slides.heading: Reception — Spring 1, Week 4
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ai" (/eɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="rain" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="rain"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Acorn Ada waits under the leaf, chin up, whenever the first raindrop of a shower slides down, ai-ai.

character.name: Ada
character.blurb: Ada is a patient little acorn who tips her cap up to catch the first drops of rain.

slides.pronunciation_note: A long, gliding sound, 'ai' as in 'rain' — let it stretch, it slides from one shape to another.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'a', then 'i', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Tip your chin up and trace one finger sliding down through the air like a raindrop, saying ai-ai.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="rain" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="rain"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: The main tricky part is the 'a', which says /o/; the 's' also sounds like 'z', not 's' — say 'woz' quietly to yourself as a clue, then write 'was'.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ee" (/iː/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="tree" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="tree"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Ellie the owl stretches up tall on her branch to see far and wide, ee-ee.

character.name: Ellie
character.blurb: Ellie is a curious owl who stretches her neck up long and tall whenever she's trying to see something far away.

slides.pronunciation_note: A long, stretched sound, 'ee' as in 'tree' — smile as you say it and hold it for a full breath.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'e' twice, close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Stretch your neck up tall, hands framing wide eyes, and hold ee-ee for a full breath.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="tree" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="tree"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "igh" (/aɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="light" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="light"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Isla the owl blinks her big eyes wide open at night, igh-igh, when the sky turns dark.

character.name: Isla
character.blurb: Isla is a night-time owl whose eyes go extra wide and round as soon as the sky darkens.

slides.pronunciation_note: A long gliding sound, 'igh' as in 'night' — three letters, one sound, glide from a wide mouth to a smile.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'i', then 'g', then 'h', close together — three letters, one sound.
slides.action: Open your eyes wide like an owl and glide one hand upward through the air, saying igh-igh.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="light" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="light"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
